content: 1. The Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services published a comprehensive report in 2019, edited by Ngo HT, Gueze M, Agard J, Arneht A, Balvanera P, Brauman K, and others, focusing on biodiversity and ecosystem services. This report was released in Bonn. 2. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) released a special report in 2019 titled Climate Change and Land, which includes a summary for policymakers. Edited by Shukla PR, Skea J, Buendia EC, Masson-Delmotte V, Portner HO, Roberts DC, and others, the report addresses climate change, desertification, land degradation, sustainable land management, food security, and greenhouse gas fluxes in terrestrial ecosystems. It was published in London. 3. In 2018, the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services published a summary for policymakers on land degradation and restoration. Edited by Scholes R, Montanarella L, Brainich A, Barger N, Brink ten B, Cantele M, and others, this report was released in Bonn. 4. The Rockefeller Foundation–Lancet Commission on Planetary Health published a report in 2015 titled Safeguarding Human Health in the Anthropocene Epoch. Authored by Whitmee S, Haines A, Beyrer C, Boltz F, Capon AG, de Souza Dias BF, and others, the report appeared in The Lancet (Volume 386, Issue 10007, Pages 1973–2028). 5. The EAT–Lancet Commission on Healthy Diets from Sustainable Food Systems published a report in 2019 titled Food in the Anthropocene. Authored by Willett W, Rockström J, Loken B, Springmann M, Lang T, Vermeulen S, and others, the report appeared in The Lancet (Volume 393, Issue 10170, Pages 447–492). 6. Afshin A, Sur PJ, Fay KA, Cornaby L, Ferrara G, Salama JS, and others conducted a systematic analysis of the health effects of dietary risks in 195 countries from 1990 to 2017. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2019 (Volume 393, Issue 10184, Pages 1958–1972) as part of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2017. 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the Global Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Noncommunicable Diseases 2013–2020 in 2013, providing a framework for addressing noncommunicable diseases globally. This report was published in Geneva. 8. Gillespie S and van den Bold M authored a report in 2017 titled Agriculture, Food Systems, and Nutrition: Meeting the Challenge, which was published by John Wiley & Sons in Oxford as part of the Global Challenges series. 9. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, in collaboration with the International Fund for Agricultural Development, UNICEF, the World Food Programme, and WHO, published The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2019 in Rome. 10. Popkin BM, Corvalan C, and Grummer-Strawn LM explored the dynamics of the double burden of malnutrition and the changing nutritional reality in a 2020 article published in The Lancet (Volume 395, Issue 10217, Pages 65–74). 11. The 2020 Global Nutrition Report, titled Action on Equity to End Malnutrition, was published by Development Initiatives in Bristol, emphasizing the need for equitable approaches to address malnutrition. 12. The United Nations System Standing Committee on Nutrition organized an expert group meeting in 2018 to discuss nutrition and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) under review, in preparation for the High-Level Political Forum. This meeting was held in Rome. 13. UNICEF, WHO, and the World Bank Group jointly published the 2020 edition of Child Malnutrition Estimates: Levels and Trends in Child Malnutrition, summarizing key findings on global child malnutrition. This report was released in New York. 14. WHO published a report in 2019 titled Nutrition in Universal Health Coverage, emphasizing the integration of nutrition into health systems. This report was released in Geneva. 15. The NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC) conducted a pooled analysis of 2,416 population-based studies, examining global trends in body mass index, underweight, overweight, and obesity from 1975 to 2016. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2017 (Volume 390, Issue 10113, Pages 2627–2642). 16. Sandifer PA, Sutton-Grier AE, and Ward BP explored the connections between nature, biodiversity, ecosystem services, and human health in a 2015 article published in Ecosystem Services (Volume 12, Pages 1–15). 17. Myers SS, Gaffikin L, Golden CD, Ostfeld RS, Redford KH, Ricketts T, and others examined the human health impacts of ecosystem alteration in a 2013 article published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (Volume 110, Issue 47, Pages 18753–18760). 18. Frison EA, Smith IF, Johns T, Cherfas J, and Eyzaguirre PB discussed the role of agricultural biodiversity in addressing hunger and malnutrition in the developing world in a 2006 article published in Food and Nutrition Bulletin (Volume 27, Issue 2, Pages 167–179). 19. Padulosi S, Thompson J, and Rudebjer PG authored a 2013 report titled Fighting Poverty, Hunger, and Malnutrition with Neglected and Underutilized Species: Needs, Challenges, and the Way Forward, published by Bioversity International in Rome. 20. Kuhnlein HV, Erasmus B, Spigelski D, and Bongiovanni R explored the food systems of indigenous peoples and their cultural, environmental, and nutritional dimensions in a 2009 report published by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the Centre for Indigenous Peoples’ Nutrition and Environment in Rome.
